salient_findings: Coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate on biopsy
key_facts: 45-year-old man
Three-week history of axillary lump
One week history of low-grade fever
Tender, non-mobile, 3 × 4 cm lymph node in the left axilla
History of hypertension
History of laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
Smoker, 30 cigarettes daily
Takes vitamin and mineral supplements
Normal or negative laboratory studies, including complete blood count, ESR, and autoantibodies
Unremarkable thoracoabdominal CT scan except for axillary lymphadenopathy
Biopsy of axillary node revealed coagulative necrosis and lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate
Investigation for mycobacteria was negative

shortlist.label: Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease
shortlist.why_kept: Matches subacute lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms and biopsy findings of coagulative necrosis and lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate

shortlist.label: Castleman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, although less common than Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of lymphadenopathy, although biopsy findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Sjögren syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause lymphadenopathy, but lack of other symptoms such as dry eyes or mouth makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Cat-scratch disease
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of lymphadenopathy, although history of cat exposure is not mentioned

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a tender, slow-growing axillary lump, low-grade fever, and a biopsy showing coagulative necrosis with frequent karyorrhexis and a lymphoplasmacytoid infiltrate is consistent with Kikuchi-Fujimoto disease, a rare, self-limiting condition characterized by lymphadenitis.

rejected.label: Castleman disease
rejected.why: Castleman disease typically presents with more systemic symptoms and abnormal laboratory findings, which are not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: The biopsy results and lack of other lymphoma symptoms make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Sjögren syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of symptoms typical of Sjögren syndrome, such as dry eyes or mouth, and autoantibodies were negative.

rejected.label: Cat-scratch disease
rejected.why: The patient's history and laboratory results do not support this diagnosis, and the biopsy findings are not consistent with cat-scratch disease.
